newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.0/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.0/9.0 percent on Tuesday morning on the back of ample liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said central bank injection of 847 billion rupiah helped keep the market flush despite tightening worries ahead of the new bank reserve requirement rate of five percent on Wednesday.

Dealers said short-term and swap rates fell across the board, but many operators were looking for directions for liquidity on Wednesday, when some five to eight trillion rupiah are expected to be drained from the market due to the new reserve rate.
One local bank dealer said money over April 16 remained well bid, with one-week money traded at 14.0 percent.

The central bank offered overnight bilateral papers to help stabilise the market on Wednesday. It offered overnight papers at six percent, one-week at 6.5 percent, two at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 11.42 percent, compared with 11.52 percent on Friday.
Bond dealers said the market remained quiet, with the yield for PLN V/A bonds staying at 14.9 percent.
